subject: physics

items.q: Two balls of different mass are dropped in a vacuum — which lands first?
items.correct: They land together; in a vacuum all objects fall with the same acceleration.
items.misconception: The heavier ball lands first because gravity pulls it harder.
items.why: Heavier means more weight but also more mass, so acceleration g is the same. Air resistance is what slows a feather in air.

items.q: A car moves at a steady speed in a straight line. What is the resultant force?
items.correct: Zero — the forces are balanced at constant velocity.
items.misconception: A forward force, because it keeps moving.
items.why: Newton's first law: constant velocity means zero resultant force; a force is only needed to change velocity.

items.q: How do mass and weight differ?
items.correct: Mass (kg) is the amount of matter; weight (N) is the gravitational force on it.
items.misconception: They are the same quantity in different units.
items.random_wrong: Weight stays the same everywhere in the universe.
items.why: Mass is constant; weight = mg changes with gravitational field strength.
